question.prompt: A train traveling from Aytown to Beetown meets with an accident after \(1\) hr. It is stopped for \(\dfrac12\) hr., after which it proceeds at four-fifths of its usual rate, arriving at Beetown \(2\) hr. late. If the train had covered \(80\) miles more before the accident, it would have been just \(1\) hr. late. The usual rate of the train is:

solutions.explanation:
The two trips have the same half-hour stop. Moving the accident \(80\) miles forward changes only the speed used on that \(80\)-mile stretch: it is covered at the usual speed instead of four-fifths of that speed. The resulting saving is \(2-1=1\) hour.

For a fixed distance, traveling at four-fifths of the speed takes five-fourths of the usual time, since distance equals speed times time. Thus the slower journey adds one fourth of the usual time. If that extra time is one hour, the usual time for \(80\) miles is
\[
1\div\frac14=4\text{ hours}.
\]
The usual speed is therefore
\[
\frac{80}{4}=20\text{ mph}.
\]
To check consistency with the original trip, the extra driving time after its accident is \(2-\tfrac12=\tfrac32\) hours. The remaining distance would normally take \(\tfrac32\div\tfrac14=6\) hours, so it is \(120\) miles. The first hour covers \(20\) miles, making the route \(140\) miles long. An accident \(80\) miles later leaves \(40\) miles, normally a two-hour stretch; its delay is \(\tfrac12+\tfrac14(2)=1\) hour, as required. Hence the answer is \(\boxed{20\text{ mph}}\), choice A.
solutions.title: Compare the stretch traveled at different speeds
